newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BIS raises dividend, benefits new members.
newsitem.headline: BIS raises dividend, benefits new members.

text.p: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) plans to raise its dividend for the 1996/97 financial year, a move that will benefit the nine countries that now have taken up their shares, said BIS, central bank to the worlds' central banks.

BIS' board of directors, comprised of central bank governors from the Group of 10 (G10) industrial nations, will propose to shareholders on June 9 that the dividend be raised by 20 francs to 280 Swiss francs per share for the year ended March 31, 1997.
The dividend will be payable on July 1 to shareholders registered in the Bank's books as of June 20, 1997.
Including the nine new BIS members, some 86 percent of BIS' share capital is owned by 41 central banks and the remaining 14 percent by private and institutional shareholders.
The 1996/97 dividend payment to the nine new members will be pro-rated, a BIS spokesman said. The new members bought BIS third tranche shares, which are only available to central banks.
As part of its move to away from mainly a European-oriented institution to a global institution, BIS last September invited nine new central banks to become members.
The new central bank members are from Hong Kong, China, Brasil, India, Korea, Mexico, Russia, Saudia Arabia and Singapore.
